stem: Ramesh introduces Kaveri to his friend saying, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is Kaveri related to Ramesh?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student places the 'only son of grandfather' one generation too low, treating him as Ramesh's brother; Kaveri then becomes Ramesh's niece instead of his sister.
Grandfather's only son = Ramesh's father; Ramesh's father's daughter = Ramesh's sister; so Kaveri is Ramesh's sister.
Student inverts the ancestor-descendant chain, reading 'only son of my grandfather' as Ramesh himself; Kaveri then becomes Ramesh's daughter.
Student skips the 'grandfather' link, reading the statement as 'daughter of my only son', making Kaveri Ramesh's granddaughter.

explanation: Trace step by step: Ramesh's grandfather -> his only son = Ramesh's father -> that man's daughter = Ramesh's sister. Kaveri is Ramesh's sister.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock the pivot first: the only son of Ramesh's grandfather is Ramesh's father. The daughter of Ramesh's father is Ramesh's sister, so Kaveri is Ramesh's sister.
explanation_sections.approach: Work the chain from the anchor outward, one link at a time. Step 1: identify who 'only son of my grandfather' is (Ramesh's father). Step 2: identify who that person's daughter is (Ramesh's sister). Do not skip or merge steps. Verify by reading the original sentence with your answer substituted back in.
explanation_sections.lesson: In blood-relation chains, resolve the innermost descriptor first. 'Only son of grandfather' is the pivot; get that right and the final relation follows in one more step.
explanation_sections.timing: About 45 seconds. Two links, each under 10 seconds to resolve. If you land on niece or daughter, you have placed the pivot one generation too low or too high; re-read step 1 only.
